id: bigtech:building a rocket is hard ast spacemobile thinks its simple:2026-11-12T18:28:22.000Z
title: Building a rocket is hard. AST SpaceMobile thinks it's "simple."
author: Eric Berger
summary_long: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a "simple" rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, "the best part is no part." Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket's development cycle. "Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines," he said of the rocket. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-12. summary_long: United Launch Alliance is set to return its Vulcan rocket to flight Friday, nine months after a solid rocket booster malfunction prompted the U.S. government to pause its use of the 215-foot-tall, non-reusable rocket. id: ai_data:internalizing investment mandates a neurosymbolic rl approac:2026-11-12T18:59:37.000Z
title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
author: Zeynep Yıldız
summary_long: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective. Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-11-12. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.

id: ai_data:agentssl can mle agents leverage unlabeled data:2026-11-12T18:59:06.000Z
title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
author: Ethan Lin
summary_long: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision. We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%. Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-11-12. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.
